definitions.gloss: back alley; back street; side lane
definitions.explanation: A narrow street or alley behind or away from the main road. Can suggest hidden charm (a tucked-away restaurant) or seediness (a dark, deserted lane), depending on context.

examples.japanese: {裏路地|うらろじ}に{迷|まよ}い{込|こ}んだ。
examples.english: I wandered into a back alley.

examples.japanese: {裏路地|うらろじ}に{隠|かく}れた{名店|めいてん}がある。
examples.english: There's a hidden gem of a restaurant in a back alley.

examples.japanese: {観光客|かんこうきゃく}で{賑|にぎ}わう{通|とお}りを{一本|いっぽん}{入|はい}ると、{静|しず}かな{裏路地|うらろじ}が{広|ひろ}がっていた。
examples.english: One street over from the tourist-packed road, a quiet back alley spread out before us.

notes:
A narrow lane behind or between main streets. In travel and food writing, {裏路地|うらろじ} often has a positive connotation — suggesting a charming, hidden-away spot. In crime or suspense contexts, it can suggest danger.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {裏路地|うらろじ}に{入|はい}る: to go into a back alley
- {裏路地|うらろじ}の{店|みせ}: a shop in a back alley
- {裏路地|うらろじ}{散歩|さんぽ}: strolling through back alleys
- {裏路地|うらろじ}に{迷|まよ}い{込|こ}む: to wander into a back alley

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {路地|ろじ}: alley, lane — more neutral; any narrow side street
- {裏通|うらどお}り: back street — slightly wider than an alley
- {横丁|よこちょう}: side street, yokocho — often a short lane with shops or bars
